  PROBLEM: The plan uses `run_attempt == 1` as a per-head re-run cap, but each newly created rerun starts with its own `run_attempt` at 1, allowing repeated reruns of the same head.
  WHY: A persistent cancellation or startup failure can therefore trigger reruns indefinitely; the planned attempt-2 test is unreachable for a rerun because the new run resets to 1, and a genuine attempt 2 is skipped earlier by the conclusion check.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- docs/plans/issue-4713-rerun-cancelled-ci-plan.md | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The plan treats `run_attempt == 1` as the per-head re-run cap, but `run_attempt` is a property of the individual workflow-run entity, not of the head's history. `POST /repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/rerun-failed-jobs` creates a brand-new run whose own `run_attempt` starts at 1, so on the next tick the script will see the new run, conclude the cap is unspent, and re-run it again — producing another new run with `run_attempt == 1`, indefinitely.
  WHY IT FAILS AT RUNTIME: A CI workflow that keeps concluding `cancelled` or `startup_failure` for the same reason every 30 minutes — a real runner outage, a missing dependency, an unparseable manifest, a quota hit, etc. — will be re-run by the sweep forever. Each tick allocates a fresh failed-jobs run (and the `startup_failure` fallback allocates a second, full re-run) until an operator notices the Telegram log lines and flips `CI_CANCELLED_AUTO_RERUN_ENABLED=false`. The only stop is the manual kill switch.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
